page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v7 is a low-memory, local-disk variant within Azure general-purpose and compute-driven infrastructure offerings. Powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, this virtual machine provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes a bundled 944 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. Hardware acceleration features include vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 support, alongside cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core compute performance, placing in the top ten percent for Geekbench single-core scores (2845.0) and stress-ng single-core testing (3791.79). Single-threaded data handling tests reflect this efficiency, with gzip compression reaching 41.33 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 18.29 GB/sec. Text processing and lightweight text generation on small language models (354.75 tokens/sec on 135M parameters) also register in the top tier. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput presents a balanced, middle-tier profile, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core result of 15608.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 32439.72.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high clock speeds with a reduced memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2. This trade-off emphasizes compute velocity and raw throughput over memory-dense caching. The bundled high-speed 944 GB NVMe SSD mitigates storage bottlenecks, delivering fast local input and output operations without separate volume attachments.

The Microsoft Azure D16alds_v7 is tailored for compute-heavy applications that do not require expansive memory footprints. Representative workloads include continuous integration and code compilation, batch image and text processing pipelines, API services, and distributed microservices with demanding local scratch-disk requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 944 GB local NVMe SSD, this instance exhibits a lean 2.0 GB per core ratio. Synthetic testing reveals top-tier single-core CPU throughput, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 2845.0, top-decile compression capabilities, and strong text processing performance. Multi-threaded metrics like PassMark CPU (32439.72) and Geekbench multi-core (15608.0) position the instance firmly in the middle tier. Because the architecture trades large memory buffers for aggressive single-thread clock frequencies and low-latency local NVMe storage, it offers cost-efficient density for compute-bound workloads. The VM is primarily suited for software build pipelines, batch data processing, API application gateways, and web serving workloads requiring fast temporary storage.
